title: SimBalance.BASE_TRAVEL_U_S is dead on arrival — nothing reads it and its comment describes a mechanism that does not exist
evidence: scripts/sim/sim_balance.gd:69: `const BASE_TRAVEL_U_S := 6.0 # nominal traversal speed at lane multiplier 1.0`. grep -rn BASE_TRAVEL_U_S across scripts/, tests/, tools/ matches ONLY this definition line (0 uses elsewhere). Actual traversal uses scripts/sim/sim_core.gd:383: `pkt.progress_milli = int(pkt.progress_milli) + SimBalance.LANE_SPEED_MILLI[int(pkt.lane)]` — there is no "lane multiplier" anywhere in the codebase.
detail: The 'one diffable balance table' carries an entry no code consumes, and its comment implies a lane-multiplier speed model that contradicts the actual fixed per-lane LANE_SPEED_MILLI table — misleading to future tuners.
recommended_fix: Delete the BASE_TRAVEL_U_S constant (or rewire traversal to derive from it) so the balance table contains only live tunables.

title: InputRouter docstrings claim classify() decides pipe-SELECT, but classify() can only return DRAW or ORBIT
evidence:
Class docstring: `## decision is factored into the static classify() so the headless suite can
## pin the contract.` Comment above the function: `## THE rule: a node hit draws, a pipe hit selects, anything else orbits.` Function body read verbatim: `static func classify(collider: Object) -> Mode:
	if collider is NodeSite:
		return Mode.DRAW
	return Mode.ORBIT`. The SELECT decision actually lives in _begin(): `_picked_pipe = flow_view.pick_pipe(screen_pos, camera)` / `_mode = Mode.SELECT if _picked_pipe >= 0 else Mode.ORBIT`.
detail: The doc tells readers the positional rule (including pipe-select) is pinned by classify(), but a pipe collider returns ORBIT from classify(); selection is geometric pick_pipe in _begin. Misleads maintainers and test authors.
recommended_fix: Reword the comments: classify() covers node-vs-not; the pipe decision is _begin()'s pick_pipe pass. Note SELECT is reached only via _begin, not classify.
